answer: Reputation is layered, not scalar: each agent accrues stake-weighted history, and every interaction is a marble added to a jar only time can fill. A new identity starts empty, so sybils cannot borrow credibility; faking depth requires sustained genuine work. Decay enforces this: idle reputation erodes on a schedule, forcing continuous participation. A dormant key loses standing, so stockpiling cheap identities yields nothing. Treat this like a fable's slow lesson rather than a comet's flash—trust grows by accretion, not announcement—so the failure mode of mass-registered fakes collapses.
